REPUBLIC OF MOZAMBIQUE

MINISTRY OF FINANCE

PROGRAM FOR STRENGTHENING GOVERNANCE AND CITIZEN SERVICE DELIVERY

MozPROSPERA — P514896

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Individual Consultants)

Technical Advisory to the Minister of Finance, Public Debt Management Reform, Development Partners’ Portfolio Monitoring and South-South Knowledge Sharing

 

Reference nr:  MZ-MF-569750-CS-INDV

Loan/Grant Number: IDA-E7400

 

1. The Government of Mozambique, through the Ministry of Finance (MF), with the support of the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank Group, is preparing the Program for Strengthening Governance and Citizen Service Delivery (MozProspera), an operation under the Program-for-Results (PforR) modality. The Ministry of Finance is the implementing agency.

2. As part of this initiative, the Government intends to apply a portion of the proceeds to the recruitment of consulting services provided by an individual consultant. The consulting services (“the Services”) will include, but are not limited to, the following activities as detailed in the Terms of Reference:

  •  Strategic technical advisory to the Minister of Finance;
  • Diagnostic and support to the public debt management reform roadmap;
  • Technical support to strengthen debt management and cash management practices;
  • Strengthening South-South cooperation and knowledge sharing;
  • Capacity building and knowledge transfer.

3. The selected consultant will be engaged under a time-based contract and remunerated at an all-inclusive daily fee rate for actual days worked and certified, whether performed remotely or in-country, up to a maximum of one hundred (100) working days. Reasonable travel and in-country subsistence expenses incurred in connection with missions to Maputo shall be reimbursed in accordance with the contract provisions. The contract shall have an initial duration of six (6) months from the date of signature and may be extended subject to satisfactory performance, Program requirements, and the availability of funds.

4. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement in Investment Project Financing), Sixth Edition, February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

5. The Ministry of Finance, now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services in the form of a curriculum vitae. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the individual consultant selection method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement in Investment Project Financing), Sixth Edition, February 2025 that can be accessed via the World Bank website at www.world bank.org/ procurement.

6. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the minimum qualification criteria for the consultancy are:

  • Master’s degree (minimum) in Economics, Public Finance, Finance, Accounting, or an equivalent field;
  • Minimum of twelve (12) years of demonstrated professional experience in public finance, of which at least eight (8) years in sovereign public debt management;
  • Prior experience in ministries of finance, debt management offices, central banks, or international financial institutions, including at senior or advisory level;
  • Demonstrated international experience: at least five (5) years of work in public debt management in countries other than the candidate’s country of nationality, including advisory assignments with governments of developing countries.
  • Demonstrated experience in providing technical and policy advice to ministers, senior government officials or executive boards on public debt matters;
  • Hands-on experience with debt recording and management systems, including data validation, reconciliation and the production of debt service projections, and with their integration with the IFMIS;
  • Experience in Sub-Saharan Africa is valued; experience in Mozambique or in Portuguese-speaking (lusophone) countries constitutes a relevant comparative advantage.
  • Working proficiency, written and oral, in English and Portuguese.  

7. Further information and the detailed Terms of Reference may be obtained upon request via the email address provided below. Expressions of Interest, comprising a cover letter and curriculum vitae, must be submitted electronically and received no later than November 9, 2026.

 

Address:                   

Ministry of Finance

449/469, Julius Nyerere Avenue, Bloc A, 11st floor

Email: procurement.mozprospera@gmail.com 

 Maputo – Mozambique
